correctness.rationale: For A=diag(a,b), a>b>0, x0=(c,s), c*s !=0, and u=||Ax0||, the normalized second vector is proportional to ((a²+beta*u)c,(b²+beta*u)s), never zero since a²!=b². Direct common-denominator subtraction gives sign(mu2-mu1)=sign(a²b²-(beta*u)²). Since b<u<a this implies uniform safe cap |beta|<=b and universal decline if |beta|>=a, with equality when |beta|u=ab. For Haar x0, W=c² is Beta(1/2,1/2), so decline event is W>b²(a²/beta²-1)/(a²-b²), yielding the inverse-cosine exact law, sharp risk inversion, and √ cusp constants. Independent SymPy exact factorization gave identically zero residual; no Monte Carlo is needed to prove probability.
